intro.title: Twelve networks. Four accounts. One phrase.
intro.narration: One MetaMask account, twelve networks: Ethereum, Linea, Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, OP Mainnet, Polygon, Monad, Arc, Bitcoin, Solana and TRON. But only four addresses — and only one private key the wallet will show you. Here is why, and how to verify every step yourself.

problem.title: Where is the rest of my wallet?
problem.narration: The wallet lists twelve networks, but the account details page shows a private key for the EVM account only. Bitcoin, Solana and TRON show an address and nothing else. It looks like a gap. It is actually the clearest window into how the whole wallet is built.

phrase-to-seed.title: A phrase is not a key.
phrase-to-seed.narration: The twelve words on your backup encode one hundred and twenty-eight bits of entropy, and BIP-39 stretches them into a sixty-four-byte seed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, two thousand and forty-eight rounds, and an optional passphrase mixed into the salt. The seed is what everything else derives from.

two-curves.title: One seed, two trees.
two-curves.narration: The seed grows two independent key trees. secp256k1 — Bitcoin, Ethereum and TRON — uses BIP-32, where child keys are added to the parent on the curve. Solana's ed25519 keys are hash seeds, not curve points, so that addition does not exist, and SLIP-0010 takes its place.

paths.title: Four paths, four keys.
paths.narration: Four derivation paths select the four branches. EVM sits at BIP-44 coin type sixty; Bitcoin uses purpose eighty-four for native SegWit; Solana is coin type five-oh-one; TRON is coin type one-ninety-five. The coin-type numbers are registered standards, and the apostrophes mark hardened derivation.

solana-slip10.title: Why Solana's apostrophes are mandatory.
solana-slip10.narration: SLIP-0010 removes the half of BIP-32 that needs curve arithmetic. A child key becomes an HMAC of the parent's private key and chain code — which works on every curve, but only for hardened derivation. That is why every Solana path segment ends in an apostrophe, and why ed25519 has no extended public keys.

encodings.title: Four ways to write an address.
encodings.narration: Each branch encodes its key differently. EVM hashes the uncompressed key with keccak-256 and keeps twenty bytes with an EIP-55 checksum. Bitcoin wraps a HASH160 of the compressed key in bech32. Solana base58-encodes the raw public key. TRON takes the same twenty bytes as EVM, prefixes forty-one, and base58checks them.

evm-shared.title: Nine networks, one key.
evm-shared.narration: The EVM branch is not the Ethereum account. Address derivation never asks which chain it is on — no chain ID, no network name — so one key produces the same address on all nine EVM networks. Same key, same address, on every EVM chain, forever.

balances.title: One address, nine ledgers.
balances.narration: What does not collapse is everything above the key. Nine networks keep nine separate ledgers and nine gas tokens: ETH on most, BNB on BNB Chain, POL on Polygon, MON on Monad. Holding ETH on Ethereum does not pay fees anywhere else, and a balance on one chain is invisible on the next.

secrets.title: Three secrets, three jobs.
secrets.narration: The MetaMask password decrypts the local vault and nothing else. The recovery phrase restores all four branches — it is the single point of failure for everything. A private key controls exactly one branch. Leak one key, lose one branch; leak the phrase, lose everything.

verify.title: Verify it yourself.
verify.narration: The derivation is fully specified by public standards — BIP-39, BIP-32, BIP-84, SLIP-0010, EIP-55 — and the repository reproduces it in about three hundred lines of TypeScript, pinned against the official specification vectors. Run npm run derive and all four accounts appear from a public test phrase.

outro.title: Twelve networks, four accounts, one phrase.
outro.narration: The code, the derivation guide, the line-by-line explainers and the trade-offs are public under the MIT license. Import the same public test phrase into any standards-compliant wallet and the four addresses match. Link in the description.
